A closed upper storey (slab 6.4 m, ceiling 10.1 m, inner wall and cross walls) runs behind the band. The ribbon has jambs at both ends, and the south-west corner no longer shows sky or ground through the building (c14_sw_slot_tele, r01_south_eye, c15_ribbon_inside_from_level, c18e_upper_storey).

Geometry check: no CLAY_GLASS lies behind any door leaf at z 1.4 m at either entrance; glass remains only above the head. Leaves are 1.2 m with stiles at 1.2 m centres, a head at 2.70-2.85 m and a transom at about 3.4 m, and no full-height mullion crosses a leaf (c05_main_entrance, c05b_entrance_square, c13_east_doors). The service door sits in a framed reveal (c23_ne_service_close). The roof entrance is now a portal cut into the west shell foot, with jambs, a head, a glazed screen and transom, and a lobby behind (c03_portal_front, c03b_portal_side_south, c03d_portal_close, c03e_portal_north, c20_portal_above).

The stair is a solid flight with a stringer face and sloping underside, and glass balustrades. It rises through a well cut in both the 5.9 m ceiling and the 6.4 m slab (ray tests show both open over y -3.9..0.6), with about 2.5 m headroom at the well edge. It lands in the closed upper storey, where a glass guard closes three sides of the well (c18_stair_foyer, c18b_stair_west_outside, c18c_stair_well_below, c18d_stair_well_above, c18e_upper_storey).
The shed-like vestibule box has been replaced by the portal in the shell foot; nothing clips the shell.

Steps and a guarded landing now take the path up to the oculus lip in the gap, so the terminus is a viewing edge (c22_lip_steps, c22b_lip_steps_top, c07b_lipgap_above). The front shell feet remain 2-3 m high, following the roof view; accepted.
The stage is now dark timber; it reads near-black where shaded, which is consistent with the dark stage in the roof reference (c08_oculus_down; builder oculus_program.png).
Planting is domed rather than spiky (c09_guard_coping, c22_lip_steps).
The service door is recessed with a head and jamb reveal (c23_ne_service_close).

An edge section at x = 0.3 m shows a 0.6 m parapet with its cap at 11.2 m, a glass guard standing on the cap (11.2-11.65 m) and a rail to 11.7 m, giving 1.1 m above the deck. There is no coplanar guard/coping overlap.
Three recessed doors lead from the foyer into the hall drum (c19b_hall_doors, c11_foyer_inside, r01_south_eye).

source_conflict_assessment: Unchanged from v007; the builder's handling is still reasonable. (1) Plan positions follow the near-orthographic roof view rather than the oblique, which places the oculus about 8 m further west. The reviewer's orthographic top render and the builder's match_top still overlay the roof reference closely, and the 31 px residual in the oblique fit remains acceptable. (2) The two 5 m storeys reproduce the reference's roughly 1:1 band-to-glazing ratio; shell rims of about 23.6 m (west) and 21.6 m (east) still give a close matched-oblique silhouette. The new closed upper storey behind the band is a plausible use of the second catalogue floor. (3) The inferred parts are now executed credibly: an opaque north-east back-of-house with a recessed service door, a hall sized to the oculus with three foyer doors, a roof-garden portal in the west shell foot with a glazed lobby, and steps to a guarded viewing landing at the lip. The lobby stair stub is the one inference that reads as incomplete from inside (N2, P2). variant_2.png: still agreed unusable. It shows a different rectilinear building with no roof garden, twin shells or oculus. Excluding it is correct, and the conflict should stay recorded for a human ruling.

findings.title: Five band fins above the north-east service door stand 8-18 cm off the cladding
findings.evidence: Exact point-to-surface distances from the GLB give 0.115, 0.170, 0.181, 0.149 and 0.078 m for the fins at azimuth 33.0-37.5 deg (centres about (37.7,24.5) to (34.9,26.8), z 6.0-11.2). Neighbouring fins are 0.016-0.019 m off and fins elsewhere are 0.000-0.02 m. Radial casts confirm that the band cladding is smooth through this arc, so the fins, not the wall, are displaced. The offset does not read at review scale (reviewer c24c_ne_fins_above with crops/ne_fins_tops.png, c24d_ne_corner_eye, r03_north_eye, r04_east_eye), so this is recorded as an unsupported-part note rather than a visible defect.
findings.required_change: Seat these five fins on the band face like their neighbours (within about 2 cm or embedded), or give them visible brackets.

findings.title: Roof-entrance lobby stair is a dead-end stub
findings.evidence: Behind the new portal's glazed screen, the lobby (x -17.9..-12.7, y -15.1..-10.9) holds a flight of ten 0.18 m risers from the 10.6 m landing down to 8.8 m. It stops against the closed shaft wall (walls 8.6-13.6 m, ceiling 13.6 m) and connects to no floor or door (reviewer c21_lobby_inside, c21b_lobby_back; GLB geometry). The builder describes it as only the top of a stair going down. It is visible only from inside the lobby; through the screen the lobby reads as an occupied, closed room (c03_portal_front, c03d_portal_close).
findings.required_change: Optional: end the visible flight at a landing with a turn or a door so the stub does not read as a dead end from inside the lobby, or keep it and record it as an abstracted stair head.

findings.title: Minor coplanar faces at new details
findings.evidence: The glass balustrade of the foyer stair well shares the vertical slab-edge faces at x = -39.7 and -37.3 (about 0.81 m2 each side, z 5.9-6.4). A north curtain-wall mullion face is flush with its glass (about 0.2 m2, x -12.2..-4.1). No flicker appears in the reviewer renders (c18c_stair_well_below, c18d_stair_well_above). The other coplanar pairs found are hidden contact faces: bases on floors, column tops, fin ends on the ribbon sill and head, the lip-step underside on the deck, and hall-door head undersides.
findings.required_change: Offset the well balustrade and that mullion face by 1-2 cm.

strengths: All four v007 P1 blockers are resolved in pixels and geometry: continuous fin grammar across the west band with a slatted ribbon; a closed upper storey with no see-through; entrances that cut the curtain wall with a proper door, head and transom section; and a supported stair rising through a cut, guarded well.
The new roof-garden portal is a real cut into the shell foot, with returns, a head, a glazed screen and an occupied lobby, replacing the shed-like box.
The lip gap now ends at a guarded viewing landing reached by steps, which makes the oculus approach legible from the garden.

Massing and identity still match both locked references at oblique, top and phone scale: rounded finned podium, two opposing bronze shells with the north notch, inner lip spiral, oculus showing raked seats, balconies, timber panels and stage, and the winding planted path.
